Quincy Williams was at it again in Week 6, tallying four solos, two assists, and one sack. Williams has started to heat up, registering two spike weeks and one splash week in his last four games. The LB15 on the season, treat Quincy as a top-12 option for a tasty Week 7 matchup against the Tennessee Titans.

Bobby Okereke was excellent in Week 6, tallying seven solos, one assist, one sack, three tackles for loss, and two passes defended. Okereke has been a strong LB2 option, recording four or more solos in three of his five contests. The LB22 through five weeks of action, treat the Panthers linebacker as a top-25 option for a plus Week 7 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Barrett Carter was excellent in Week 5, reeling off five solos, six assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Carter has recorded five or more solos in three of his five games, but managed just two solos in the other two, keeping him in LB2 territory. Tap him as a top-20 option for Week 7.

Nate Landman was excellent in Week 6, tallying six solos and four assists. Landman has one splash week and two spike weeks on the season, helping keep him in the top-20 mix. He has not been as productive, relative to others, as fantasy managers may have hoped, but is still a rock-solid LB2 with weekly LB1 upside. Treat him as just that for a plus Week 7 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders.

Pete Werner stepped up in Week 6, racking up five solos, six assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended on 100 percent of the snaps. Werner now has two spike weeks to his name and is playing a full-time role with Kaden Elliss sidelined. An LB3 when Elliss is healthy, and he is splitting snaps with Danny Stutsman, Werner is a high-end LB2 option with Kaden injured. Werner has recorded four or more solos in three of his last five games. Treat Werner as a top-20 option until Elliss returns, at which point he will go back to being a top-36 option.

Demetrius Knight was excellent in Week 5, reeling off five solos, three assists, and two tackles for loss. Knight has two spike weeks and one splash week to his name, making him a top-25 option, especially during the byes. Treat him as such for Week 7.

Jaden Dugger impressed again in Week 6, notching eight solos and three assists on 100 percent of the snaps. Dugger was a hit from a fantasy perspective, but his struggles in coverage ensure that he won't be unseating Dre Greenlaw (suspended for Week 6) anytime soon. The back-to-back spike weeks as a starter make him a dynasty stash for 2027 and beyond, but it will take another suspension or injury before Dugger is fantasy relevant again this season. Look elsewhere for Week 7.

Henry To'oTo'o returned to action in Week 6, posting three solos, three assists, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. To'oTo'o had been sidelined since Week 1 with Jake Hansen filling in for him. To'oTo'o becomes an immediate LB3 candidate who will return to the LB2 conversation once he gets his legs back under him and shows some consistency. Tap the Texans linebacker as a top-30 option for a tasty Week 7 matchup against the New York Giants.

Derrick Barnes was excellent in Week 5, racking up three solos, two assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Barnes has been elite this season with three spike weeks and one splash week to his name, but is still good to count as more of a top-15 option than a top-10 one due to posting a dud in the other game. Treat him as such for Week 7.

Ty'Ron Hopper was solid in Week 6, generating three solos, two assists, and one pass defended on 42 percent of the snaps. Hopper looked like the Packer who was going to lead the position group in snaps alongside Zaire Franklin, but in Week 6, Isaiah McDuffie played 55 percent of the snaps. It appears that both Hopper and McDuffie will rotate in place of the injured Edgerrin Cooper, essentially cannibalizing each other's fantasy values in the process. They both will provide some start-worthy stat lines over the course of the rest of the season, but predicting who will when becomes a futile exercise as long as they are in a platoon-type situation. Keep him stashed in deeper formats, but look elsewhere for Week 7.

Nick Herbig finally showed up in Week 6, racking up six solos, two sacks, and three tackles for loss. Herbig is a clear backup to T.J. Watt and Alex Highsmith but often gets enough snaps to make an impact, as he can play against both the run and the pass. The sacks were the first of the season for Herbig, who has been solid for a bench piece and has started to heat up during the byes. Tap Herbig as a DL3 with a DL4 floor for a tasty Week 7 matchup against the New Orleans Saints.

Jeremiah Trotter stepped up in Week 6, racking up four solos, two assists, and 0.5 sacks on 36 percent of the snaps. Trotter saw an expanded role in Week 6, with Jihaad Campbell being demoted due to issues in coverage. This may be a long-term ascension as the Eagles are looking for a spark on defense and are tired of opposing teams targeting Jihaad in coverage.  Trotter becomes an immediate LB3 with LB2 upside as long as he is receiving starter snaps, and can jump into the LB2 conversation once we are certain his snaps will not fluctuate too wildly on a week-to-week basis. Tap Trotter as a top-30 option for a tasty Week 7 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys on Monday Night Football.

David Walker stepped up in Week 6, tallying four solos, three assists, two sacks, and two tackles for loss on 32 percent of the snaps. Walker is now up to four sacks on the season with at least one sack in three of his last five games. Walker has been the Buccaneers' most productive edge player but has yet to attain starter-level snaps. That could change in a hurry, but for now we can only trust the Bucs edge rusher as a flex2 type as opposed to the DL3 type his sack production and obvious talent suggest.

Kyle Hamilton stayed toasty in Week 6, racking up six solos, one assist, and three tackles for loss. The Ravens do-it-all safety has registered five straight spike weeks and is locked in as a top three option. If you need proof of an elite floor when he's rolling, look no further than his six or more solos in four of his last five games. Start Hamilton everywhere.

Evan Williams stayed hot in Week 6, notching five solos, one assist, one interception, and one pass defended. Williams has been on absolute fire to open the season, seemingly capturing the elusive consistency that plagued his 2025 IDP campaign. Now locked in as a weekly elite play, Williams should be considered a top-three option. Start the DB1 overall in fantasy points everywhere for Week 7 and beyond.

The New contract narrative stayed alive and well in Week 6, with Budda Baker going off with four solos, two assists, one sack, two tackles for loss, and one pass defended. Budda has been a man on a mission and is enjoying a career renaissance in his age-30 season. The DB3 through six weeks of action, Baker needs to be counted as a top-five option, period. Start him everywhere for a plus Week 7 matchup against the Denver Broncos.

Quentin Lake was excellent in Week 6, tallying six solos, one assist, one interception, and one pass defended. Lake has recorded six or more solos in three of his six contests, which directly coincide with his two spike weeks and one splash week. Continue to treat Lake as a locked-in top-five option, including this week against the Las Vegas Raiders.

Jeremy Chinn stepped up in Week 6, tallying nine solos and one assist. Chinn has recorded two spike weeks and one splash week on the season, pushing him up to DB6 on the season. Count Chinn as a DB1 play for a plus Week 7 matchup against a banged-up Los Angeles Rams.

Nick Emmanwori showed out in Week 6, tallying four solos, three assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Nick has recorded one spike week and one splash week in his last three games, re-cementing himself as a top-five option, despite some new and old names joining the fray in that weekly discussion. Start Emmanwori everywhere.

Cooper DeJean stayed hot in Week 6, racking up six solos and one tackle for loss. DeJean has registered three consecutive spike weeks, vaulting him up to DB12 on the season despite a slower start than expected. Cooper is once again safe to count as a top-15 option regardless of opponent. Treat him as such for a plus Week 7 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys on Monday Night Football.

Kamari Lassiter stayed hot in Week 6, tallying six solos, two assists, and one pass defended. Lassiter has recorded three spike weeks in his last four games, helping bump him up to DB14 status on the season. An elite DB2 option despite playing outside corner, Lassiter should be started everywhere for a tasty Week 7 matchup against 'Nine' and the New York Giants.

Amani Hooker stayed hot in Week 6, generating seven solos, six assists, one interception, and one pass defended for his first splash week of the season. Hooker has been one of the most consistent options at the position all season, and the monster week vaulted him up to DB10 on the season. Tap Hooker as a top-15 option during the byes, and possibly beyond. Treat him as such for a plus Week 7 matchup against the Cleveland Browns.

Caleb Downs stepped up in Week 6, tallying six solos and six assists. Downs has posted three spike weeks, helping boost him to DB36 on the season. There will be some inconsistency for the rookie safety, but he is showing the type of upside that can put him in the DB2 mix sooner rather than later. For now, treat him as a top-30 option for a tasty Week 7 matchup against a decimated Philadelphia Eagles team.

Chamarri Conner stepped up in Week 6, tallying four solos, one sack, and one tackle for loss. It was Chamarri's second contest of the season and may be a sign that he is ready to start rolling for the Chiefs and IDP managers alike. For now, treat him as more of a high-end DB2 than a DB1, including this week against a struggling Seattle Seahawks team.

Jordan Battle was excellent in Week 5, tallying five solos, two assists, two interceptions, and two passes defended. The DB12 through five weeks of play due to the splash week and two spike weeks, Battle has recorded four or more solos in three of his five games. There will be some inconsistency, but the Bengals safety is an easy top-15 option during the byes. Treat him as such for a plus Week 7 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens.

Jalen Ramsey went berserk in Week 6, exploding for nine solos, one assist, two sacks, and four tackles for loss. Ramsey had been rock solid up to this point, but is now the DB6 in total fantasy points. Jalen is a solid DB3 option during the byes, especially after the monster Week 6 production. Tap Ramsey as a top-36 option for a plus Week 7 matchup against the New Orleans Saints in Paris.

Jacob Parrish stayed hot in Week 6, racking up five solos, one assist, one tackle for loss, and two passes defended. Parrish has registered three straight spike weeks, with at least five solos in each of those contests. On the season as a whole, Parrish has recorded four or more solos in four of his five games played. The Buccaneers corner is an easy CB1/DB3 for Week 7, and should be treated as one until he cools down.

Jevon Holland stepped up in Week 6, recording six solos, three assists, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. Holland should have more spike weeks than in past seasons, but may still be a peaks-and-valleys type of DB3 with obvious DB1 upside. Treat Holland as a top-30 option for Week 7 and beyond.

Javon Bullard showed up on Sunday Night Football, recording four solos, two assists, and three passes defended. Jamel Dean stepped up in Week 6, reeling off two solos, two assists, one interception, and six passes defended. It was the first spike week of the season for Dean, but it is worth noting that he forced two fumbles in back-to-back games to start the season. Still, Dean is no more than a CB2 with 16+ team DB5 appeal. Look elsewhere for Week 7.

Ja'Quan McMillan stepped up in Week 6, tallying five solos, one sack, one tackle for loss, one interception, and two passes defended. McMillan has been seeing increased snaps with Pat Surtain (ankle) sidelined and Riley Moss also dealing with injury issues, and has responded with a spike week and a splash week in back-to-back games.

Roger McCreary was excellent in Week 5, racking up five solos, one assist, and six passes defended. McCreary has two spike weeks under his belt, keeping him in the CB1/2 conversation while he's hot. He has recorded four or more solos in three of his five games, suggesting that he has a path to DB3 value outside of four team byes. Tap McCreary as a CB1/DB3 option for a plus Week 7 matchup against the Green Bay Packers.

Josh Wallace stepped up in Week 6, tallying five solos, three assists, one tackle for loss, and two passes defended. Wallace has recorded two spike weeks in his last four games, putting him in the CB2 mix for the byes, and potentially beyond. Treat Wallace as just that for Week 7, but those in DB leagues are advised to look elsewhere.

Brandon Cisse was excellent in Week 6, racking up four solos, one interception, and two passes defended. Cisse has recorded four or more solos in four of his six games, making him a CB1 with DB3 upside during the byes. The DB41 on the season, Cisse should be started where needed for a plus Week 7 matchup against the Detroit Lions.

Martin Emerson stepped up in Week 6, racking up seven solos, one tackle for loss, two interceptions, and four passes defended. Emerson stepped in when Kool-Aid McKinstry left the game and responded by winning NFC Player of the Week honors. Emerson is a CB2 option if McKinstry misses Week 7, but will go back to waiver wire material if the veteran is active.

Kris Abrams-Draine showed up in Week 6, racking up four solos, two assists, one forced fumble, one interception, and three passes defended. Abrams-Draine doesn't see the field much when both Pat Surtain and Riley Moss are healthy, but has looked roster-worthy in CB leagues while one or both remain hobbled. He has not done enough to be a DB league consideration despite the strong outing, so look elsewhere for your Week 7 DB3/4.

Tony Adams was excellent in Week 6, reeling off eight solos, four assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. Adams is the top safety backup for the Titans and filled in this week for the injured Kevin Winston. Adams has DB3 upside with Winston sidelined, especially during the byes. Treat him as such for a plus Week 7 matchup against the Cleveland Browns.
